CNS & Special Pathology

CNS pathology - stroke, brain tumors, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's disease, and nervous system pathology.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe common CNS pathologies
  • Explain stroke types and pathology
  • Describe Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease pathology

In simple terms

Central nervous system (CNS) pathology deals with diseases of the brain and spinal cord. Common conditions include stroke, brain tumors, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and multiple sclerosis. Nurses care for patients with neurological conditions and must understand the pathology to provide appropriate care.

Common CNS disorders

Disorder Cause/Features Key signs
Ischemic stroke Blood vessel blockage in brain Sudden weakness, facial droop, slurred speech
Hemorrhagic stroke Blood vessel rupture in brain Sudden severe headache, vomiting, decreased consciousness
Alzheimer’s disease Neurodegenerative, amyloid plaques Memory loss, cognitive decline, disorientation
Parkinson’s disease Dopamine-producing neuron loss Tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability
Brain tumor Abnormal cell growth in brain Headache, seizures, focal neurological deficits
Multiple sclerosis Autoimmune demyelination Fatigue, vision problems, weakness, numbness

Nursing care

  • Stroke assessment - use FAST (Face, Arms, Speech, Time); position head elevated 30°; monitor swallow before oral intake
  • Parkinson’s disease - give levodopa on time; assist with mobility; encourage independence; monitor for dyskinesia
  • Multiple sclerosis - prevent fatigue (heat intolerance); assist with mobility; monitor for bladder/bowel dysfunction
  • Brain tumor - monitor for increased intracranial pressure; seizure precautions; pain management
  • Patient education - teach about condition, medications, fall prevention, when to seek help

🔴 Stroke = medical emergency

Stroke = medical emergency. FAST = Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services. Time = brain - every minute counts.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Stroke assessment - use FAST (Face, Arms, Speech, Time); note time of symptom onset; position head elevated 30°; monitor swallow before oral intake
  • Parkinson’s disease - give levodopa on time; assist with mobility; encourage independence; monitor for dyskinesia
  • Multiple sclerosis - prevent fatigue (heat intolerance); assist with mobility; monitor for bladder/bowel dysfunction
  • Brain tumor - monitor for increased intracranial pressure; seizure precautions; pain management
  • Patient education - teach about condition, medications, fall prevention, when to seek help

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Stroke (CVA) = blood vessel blockage/rupture in brain; FAST = Face, Arms, Speech, Time.
  2. Parkinson's disease = dopamine-producing neuron loss; tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability.
  3. Multiple sclerosis = autoimmune demyelination; fatigue, vision problems, weakness, numbness.
  4. Brain tumor = abnormal cell growth in brain; headache, seizures, focal neurological deficits.
  5. Seizure precautions = padded side rails, suction, oxygen; do not restrain; do not put anything in mouth.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Stroke = medical emergency; note time of symptom onset; position head elevated 30°; monitor swallow before oral intake.
  2. Levodopa for Parkinson's: give on time; monitor for dyskinesia.
  3. MS: prevent fatigue (heat intolerance); assist with mobility; monitor for bladder/bowel dysfunction.
  4. Brain tumor: monitor for increased intracranial pressure; seizure precautions; pain management.

📌 Memory trick

Stroke = FAST - Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services. Time = brain.

60-second revision

  • Neurological disorders: stroke, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, brain tumor, epilepsy.
  • Stroke = FAST; medical emergency; time = brain.
  • Parkinson’s = tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia; levodopa on time.
  • MS = fatigue, weakness; prevent heat intolerance.
  • Epilepsy = seizures; seizure precautions; do not restrain; do not put anything in mouth.
  • Brain tumor = monitor for increased intracranial pressure; seizure precautions.

Test yourself

Stroke (CVA) =

Answer: B. Stroke = blood vessel blockage or rupture in the brain causing brain cell death.

Parkinson's disease is characterised by:

Answer: A. Parkinson's disease = tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia (slowness of movement), postural instability.

Multiple sclerosis is:

Answer: A. Multiple sclerosis = autoimmune demyelination of nerves in the brain and spinal cord.

During a seizure, do NOT:

Answer: B. During a seizure, do not restrain; do not put anything in mouth; position on side; protect from injury.

Brain tumour signs include:

Answer: A. Brain tumour = abnormal cell growth in brain; symptoms include headache, seizures, focal neurological deficits.
